results.title: Model-based systems engineering in NASA facility requirements development
results.abstract: A functional requirements document was developed to guide a modernization project for the power supply of the NASA Ames Arc Jet Complex, considering the various stakeholder's desires for improvements, interfaces with existing equipment, and best practices in space systems engineering. The team chose to use a model-based systems engineering (MBSE) methodology implemented through SysML[1]. This approach enabled the team to do all the necessary steps in a single source of authority, including printing the latest version of the document deliverable through an automated report with a customized template. The team utilized the model to capture stakeholder input, create a multi-dimensional concept of operations and functional decomposition from the desired functionality of the system, directly trace the requirements to all this information, and track the development and traceability of the requirements. By tracing requirements, most of which were derived from a more “bottoms-up” detailed view of the existing system, to the modelled “top-down” stakeholder input on desired improvements, engineers could see gaps in requirements development or functional definition. The different sources of functional requirements were easy to connect in a model and allowed thorough requirements development with detailed traceability. By updating system definition and requirement elements in the model, the team could immediately see which other elements it might affect. The work was completed in a few months. Tasks of similar scope developing a requirements flow and the document management process in the last 10 years without MBSE have taken about a year.
